description: Worked as a qualified conference interpreter and translator after completing her studies at the Zurich interpreters' school (DOZ).

organization: Kaufmännische Berufsschulen St. Gallen and Wil
description: Taught at the commercial vocational schools in St. Gallen and Wil; completed a part-time teaching qualification (Berufsmittelschullehrerin) at the University of Fribourg from 1994 to 1996.

role: Member of the municipal parliament of Wil (and president 1997)
description: Member of the Wil municipal parliament; served as its president in 1997. From 1997 also president of the cantonal FDP party.
Deputy in the cantonal parliament (Kantonsrat) of St. Gallen.

role: Cantonal Councillor, Head of Security and Justice Department
organization: Government Council (Regierungsrat) of the Canton of St. Gallen
description: Member of the St. Gallen cantonal government for twelve years, heading the Security and Justice Department. Government president in 2006-2007 and 2011-2012. Chaired the Conference of Cantonal Justice and Police Directors (KKJPD) 2010-2012. Built a reputation as a hardliner on asylum, immigration and security.

role: Member of the Council of States (Ständerat), President 2017-2018
organization: Federal Assembly of Switzerland (Council of States), canton St. Gallen
description: Represented St. Gallen in the Council of States from late 2011/2012 until her move to the Federal Council. Member of committees on economic affairs and taxation, social security and health, and foreign affairs, and president of the EFTA/EU delegation (2018). President of the Council of States in 2017-2018.

role: Federal Councillor, Head of the Federal Department of Justice and Police (FDJP)
description: Headed the Federal Department of Justice and Police, succeeding Simonetta Sommaruga. Focused on rigorous implementation of the Dublin asylum framework, security legislation and corporate/civil law reform.

role: Federal Councillor, Head of the Federal Department of Finance (FDF/DFF)
description: Heads the Federal Department of Finance, succeeding Ueli Maurer. Led the federal response to the March 2023 Credit Suisse crisis and the UBS takeover, the implementation of the OECD/G20 minimum tax, and federal budget policy under the debt brake. Vice President of Switzerland 2024; President of the Confederation 2025.
